conviction_note: The findings sum to a small positive (+0.3): Montage's 2026-10-20 pre-release shows DDR5 interface-chip demand up 20.9% QoQ in Q3 with Q4 'rising further', against a name 48% off its high, 14% down in 20 days and close to its 52-week low. That is offset by a reaction function that has sold the last four prints (-9.0, -21.3, -13.4, -8.7), a royalty-led Q2 beat, a stepped-down Q3 royalty guide and a bear case on memory supply that is still live. So p_up is 53, barely off a coin flip, and abs_move is 12, close to the 13.1% the options imply. Both measurements are near zero and agree in sign, with neither strong.
bar: Q3 revenue consensus $213.2M (Benzinga; a second Benzinga page shows $213.4M) and non-GAAP EPS consensus $0.76 (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/rmbs/earnings-forecasts). Both sit inside the company guide of $210-216M revenue, $110-116M product, $69-75M royalties, $25-31M contract/other and EPS $0.75-0.82 on 110M diluted shares (https://www.rambus.com/second-quarter-2026-financial-results/, 2026-07-27). The EPS consensus is below the guide midpoint of $0.785. Q4 revenue consensus is about $224.8-226.6M per Benzinga, roughly +5.5% QoQ. No product-revenue consensus was found. The guide is a company document, so the bar is sourced and the sizes are not capped for it.
positioning_check: Short interest is about 4.1M shares with 1.3 days to cover as of the 2026-08-19 settlement (https://equibles.com/stocks/rmbs/shortinterest). Benzinga's sentiment page, updated 2026-09-24, shows a 7.6% short float, labelled 'rising' (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/RMBS/short-interest). The two sources disagree, but neither is a crowded short, and no October figure was found. Skew is +3.17 vol points (25d put IV over call), so downside is paid but modestly. Put/call open-interest ratio is 0.82. The tape is -13.9% over 20 days and -5.1% over 5, -48.5% from the 52-week high and +10.3% off the low. AAII has the stock down 17.7% in October and logs one downgrade and one upgrade in the month to Oct 23, firms unnamed (https://www.aaii.com/investingideas/article/541227-why-rambus-inc8217s-rmbs-stock-is-down-661).

findings.finding: Montage Technology (688008.SS), the main DDR5 RCD/interface-chip competitor, pre-announced Q3 2026 on 2026-10-20: interconnect-chip revenue about RMB 2.047bn, +20.9% QoQ and +49.3% YoY, at 68.0-68.5% gross margin (up 0.6-1.1pt QoQ). Drivers it named: server-CPU demand from AI inference/agents, a large rise in DDR5 interface and companion-chip shipments, and a higher mix of Gen3/4/5 RCD. It expects demand to 'rise further' in Q4. Rambus guided Q3 product revenue to $110-116M, +14% QoQ and about +21% YoY at the midpoint (Q3 2025 product was $93.3M). Industry units were therefore not choked by DRAM supply in Q3, which supports a product print at or above the top of the guide and a firm Q4 product guide. Montage again grew faster than Rambus (+49% vs about +21% YoY), which feeds the share-loss bear case. The finding is sized net of that.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Product revenue and the guide are what this stock trades on. Q1 2026 missed on product (an OSAT issue) and fell -21.3% with the Baird downgrade. Q2 product came in at $99.2M, inside the $95-101M guide, with a Q3 product guide of +14% QoQ, and the stock fell -9.0%. The last product-led upside was Q2 2025 (+13.9%).
findings.why_not_priced: It came from a Shanghai STAR-board pre-announcement in Chinese. Montage rose 6.1% that day, but RMBS is -5.1% over the five sessions since and has not traded on the read. If US holders had priced it, RMBS would have bounced from its Oct 16 low ($87.25) on Oct 20-21; it is still at $87.90.
findings.independence: Same pre-release is reported by https://m.rccaijing.com/news-7518552184561792701.html (2026-10-21, same document, counted once). The server DDR5 bit-growth series cited by Fusion Worldwide (Baird via TrendForce: server DDR5 about +20% in 3Q26, +15-20% in 4Q26; https://info.fusionww.com/blog/prerel-server-rdimm-supply-remains-squeezed-with-vendor-offers-sharply-reduced) points the same way and is a proxy.

findings.finding: DRAM supply is expected to stay tight into 2027-2028. Per Reuters via TrendForce, 2026-10-08, Samsung and Micron both expect tight memory supply through 2028. TrendForce sees 2027 RDIMM bit supply growth of only 15-20%, below server-CPU growth. This is the exact mechanism of the April Baird downgrade: a volume-driven RCD model loses unit growth when RDIMM supply is constrained, with Baird modelling RDIMM units +20% in 2026 slowing to 12-15% in 2027. The risk sits on the Q4 guide and on 2027 commentary. A small offset: TrendForce reports systems shifting from 96/128GB to 32/64GB RDIMMs from 3Q26, which means more modules, and so more RCDs, per bit.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Baird supply-constraint thesis came with the -21.3% reaction on 2026-04-28. In July the stock fell -9.0% on a beat as the forward commentary read 'in line'.
findings.why_not_priced: It is mostly priced: the stock is 48% off its high, largely on this thesis. What may not be priced is how Rambus itself frames 2027 unit growth on this call. If it were fully in the price, the skew would be steeper than +3.2.
findings.independence: Baird's April note: https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/rambus-shares-crater-revenue-miss-173700183.html (2026-04-28). TrendForce on the module-density shift and 2027 RDIMM bit supply: https://iconnect007.com/article/150723/server-dram-contract-prices-to-rise-1318-qoq-in-3q26-amid-longterm-price-caps/150720/pcb (2026-07-09, published before the Q3 guide, so partly embedded in it). The Montage finding above cuts the other way for Q3 units.

findings.finding: The Q2 2026 beat was royalty-led. Royalties were $84.2M against a $72-78M guide, while product was $99.2M, inside its $95-101M guide. The Q3 royalty guide steps down to $69-75M, so Q3 total-revenue growth has to come from product (+$14M QoQ at the midpoint). The stock sold the royalty-led beat by -9.0%. A Q3 beat carried by royalties or contract revenue again would likely be treated the same way.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: revenue $207.4M against $199.3M consensus (+4%), EPS $0.77, stock -9.0%. Q1 2026: revenue miss (-5%), stock -21.3%.
findings.why_not_priced: This is about the quality of the beat, not new information. It matters because consensus revenue ($213.2M) can be beaten on lumpy licensing without the product line moving, and the market has shown it discounts that.
findings.independence: Q1 2026 line detail and the reaction: https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/rambus-shares-crater-revenue-miss-173700183.html. Q2 consensus figure: https://wtop.com/news/2026/07/rambus-q2-earnings-snapshot/

findings.finding: A $100M accelerated share repurchase with Mizuho was entered 2026-08-04, with about 796k shares delivered up front and completion expected by end of Q3. It came after the Q3 EPS guide, which assumed 110M diluted shares. The weighted share count is therefore about 0.6-0.8% lower than guided, worth roughly half a cent of non-GAAP EPS, a mechanical tailwind against the $0.76 consensus.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print turned on share count.
findings.why_not_priced: It is small and public. The point is only that the EPS guide was set before it and so excludes it.

findings.finding: Positioning into the print is washed out. The stock is -13.9% over 20 days and -17.7% in October, 10% above its 52-week low and 48% below its high. Short interest is not crowded (about 4.1M shares, 1.3 days to cover, Aug 19). The October slide was attributed to a sector-wide semiconductor/AI selloff with no company news (Oct 12). StoneX kept its Buy and $165 target that day.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The last four prints all fell (-8.7, -13.4, -21.3, -9.0) from various starting points. The July -9.0% came after the stock had rallied into the print.
findings.why_not_priced: This is what the price is. It is filed only because the run-up is part of the bar a beat or miss is measured against. The skew (+3.2) and four straight negative reactions say the market still leans down, so it is sized small.

findings.finding: There is accounting-leadership turnover. The CFO left in February 2026 and the interim CFO, Chief Accounting Officer John Allen, gave notice of retirement on 2026-08-31. William Taulbee, ex-Western Digital Chief Audit Executive, became CAO on 2026-09-08. The 8-K states no disagreement. A new CFO (Sumeet Gagneja, ex-AMD data-center CFO) is on his second print.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public and minor. A new finance team on its second guide may guide more conservatively, which is the only path to the print.

baseline_tension: Mixed. The washed-out run-up and the Montage read lean against the +3.2 put skew and the four straight negative reactions, but only weakly. That is why p_up sits at 53 and not higher.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (a verified fact is not a predicted reaction; this name sold its last four prints): Montage finding cut from +1.0 to +0.8, and p_up from 54 to 53
Lesson 5 (a drawdown is not evidence; a proxy is filed small): positioning finding cut from +0.5 to +0.3
Royalty-quality, memory-supply, ASR and CAO findings left unchanged; the bar is the company guide, so no cap applies (lesson 6)
